## Explicit SSP Runge-Kutta stages in Shu-Osher form (`integration/type`) {#sec-ch07-rk}

### Summary

The time integrator is pyharp's `IntegratorImpl`. snapy calls it once per stage to average three states: the state
at the start of the step, the state of the current stage and the full-step tendency that the stage computed. All
four tableaux are strong-stability-preserving (SSP) Runge-Kutta schemes in Shu-Osher form, so every stage is a
convex combination of the step-start state and a forward-Euler step. A property that a forward-Euler step keeps
under a time-step limit, such as the nonnegativity of a species density under the positivity limiter of
@sec-ch08, the stage keeps under the same limit scaled by the SSP coefficient.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Advances the state over one step in one to four stages, each a convex combination; @eq-ch07-rk-stage.

**Data.** Reads $\mathbf U^n$, the stage state and $\Delta t\,\mathcal L$, ghosts included; writes the next stage state.

**Placement.** The whole step: stage 0 saves $\mathbf U^n$, and each stage ends with the average.

**Activation.** `integration/type`: `rk1` (or `euler`), `rk2`, `rk3` (default), `rk3s4`; read by pyharp.

**Guarantee / limits.** Order 1, 2, 3, 3; SSP with $c_{\mathrm{SSP}}$ = 1, 1, 1, 2; one `cfl`[^rg-b85b53c55d48] for every type.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch07-rk-tests; `test_forcing.release`, `test_straka`, `rk_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C7]`.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathcal Y$ [-] is the scalar of the test equation $\mathrm d\mathcal Y/\mathrm dt=\mathcal G\mathcal Y$,
$\mathcal G$ [s$^{-1}$] its constant rate and $\mathcal Z=\mathcal G\Delta t$ [-]; $\Delta t_{\mathrm{FE}}$ [s] is the
largest forward-Euler step that keeps a convex functional from growing; $c^{(s)}_{\mathrm{FE}}$ [-] is the forward-Euler fraction of
stage $s$ and $c_{\mathrm{SSP}}=\min_s c^{(s)}_{\mathrm{FE}}$ [-] the SSP coefficient, the factor by which a scheme's step may exceed
$\Delta t_{\mathrm{FE}}$ with the same guarantee; $\zeta_n=n(\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2)/(1-n\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2)$ [-] bounds
the relative error of $n$ roundings. $C$[^rg-2b93cd28ee3b] stays the Courant number of @sec-ch07-cfl.

The state averaged is $\mathbf U$[^rg-15d7eb0a1f99] with its ghosts ($\rho_{\mathrm d}$[^rg-a3c1b56ee687], $\rho_n$[^rg-216a5cf9b341], $m_a$, $E$[^rg-071a0a3e4354], total-mass basis) and the
passive-scalar densities $\rho_{\mathrm d}r_n$ (dry-mass basis). The type is read from YAML[^rg-0ebf34f7decd] with default `rk3`; an
unknown type throws. The step-start registers and the stage index that the VIC needs are set by snapy's stage
driver.

The steps of one time step, from reconstruction to the final update: the step size is set once (@sec-ch07-cfl);
then each stage reconstructs the face states, solves the Riemann problems, limits the fluxes, forms the flux
divergence and adds the forcings and the vertical implicit correction (`HydroImpl::forward`), adds the user stage
forcings, takes the average of @eq-ch07-rk-stage with the conserved limiter and refills any solid cells; on the
last stage only, the phase adjustment and the gravity-work fixer follow when they are on; and every stage ends by
filling the physical ghosts. @sec-ch02-laws lists the same order with the code that runs it, and @sec-ch01-hydro
follows one increment through it.

### Derivation

Let $\mathcal L(\mathbf U)$ be the semi-discrete right-hand side, so that the stage tendency is
$\Delta\mathbf U = \Delta t\,\mathcal L(\mathbf U)$, the full-step increment that `HydroImpl::forward` returns
(@sec-ch04, @sec-ch09). With $\mathbf U^{(0)}=\mathbf U^n$, stage $s$ forms

$$
\mathbf U^{(s+1)} = w_0^{(s)}\,\mathbf U^n + w_1^{(s)}\,\mathbf U^{(s)} + w_2^{(s)}\,\Delta t\,\mathcal L(\mathbf U^{(s)}) ,
$$ {#eq-ch07-rk-stage}

implemented as `pintg->forward(stage, _hydro_u0, hydro_u, fut_hydro_du)`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}), whose body is the linear combination of `IntegratorImpl::forward`
([`pyharp integrator.cpp:101-122`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L101-L122)). The weights $(w_0^{(s)},w_1^{(s)},w_2^{(s)})$ of each stage are set in the
`IntegratorImpl` constructor ([`pyharp integrator.cpp:33-85`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L33-L85)):

| type | stage 1 | stage 2 | stage 3 | stage 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rk1` | $(0,1,1)$ | | | |
| `rk2` | $(0,1,1)$ | $(\tfrac12,\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$ | | |
| `rk3` | $(0,1,1)$ | $(\tfrac34,\tfrac14,\tfrac14)$ | $(\tfrac13,\tfrac23,\tfrac23)$ | |
| `rk3s4` | $(\tfrac12,\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$ | $(0,1,\tfrac12)$ | $(\tfrac23,\tfrac13,\tfrac16)$ | $(0,1,\tfrac12)$ |

: Stage weights $(w_0^{(s)},w_1^{(s)},w_2^{(s)})$ of the four integrator types. {#tbl-ch07-rk-weights}

*Order.* On $\mathrm d\mathcal Y/\mathrm dt=\mathcal G\mathcal Y$ a stage of @eq-ch07-rk-stage maps
$\mathcal Y\mapsto w_0^{(s)}\mathcal Y^n+(w_1^{(s)}+w_2^{(s)}\mathcal Z)\,\mathcal Y$, starting from $\mathcal Y^{(0)}=\mathcal Y^n$.
Multiplying the stages out with the weights of @tbl-ch07-rk-weights (every value below is a multiple of $\mathcal Y^n$):

1. `rk1`: $\mathcal Y^{(1)}=1+\mathcal Z$.
2. `rk2`: $\mathcal Y^{(2)}=\tfrac12+\tfrac12(1+\mathcal Z)^2=1+\mathcal Z+\tfrac12\mathcal Z^2$.
3. `rk3`: $\mathcal Y^{(2)}=\tfrac34+\tfrac14(1+\mathcal Z)^2=1+\tfrac12\mathcal Z+\tfrac14\mathcal Z^2$, and
   $\mathcal Y^{(3)}=\tfrac13+\tfrac23(1+\mathcal Z)(1+\tfrac12\mathcal Z+\tfrac14\mathcal Z^2)=1+\mathcal Z+\tfrac12\mathcal Z^2+\tfrac16\mathcal Z^3$.
4. `rk3s4`: $\mathcal Y^{(1)}=1+\tfrac12\mathcal Z$, $\mathcal Y^{(2)}=(1+\tfrac12\mathcal Z)^2$,
   $\mathcal Y^{(3)}=\tfrac23+\tfrac13(1+\tfrac12\mathcal Z)^3$, and
   $\mathcal Y^{(4)}=(1+\tfrac12\mathcal Z)\,\mathcal Y^{(3)}=1+\mathcal Z+\tfrac12\mathcal Z^2+\tfrac16\mathcal Z^3+\tfrac1{48}\mathcal Z^4$.
5. The first three agree with $e^{\mathcal Z}$ to the order of the scheme. `rk3s4` agrees to $\mathcal Z^3$ and its
   $\mathcal Z^4$ coefficient is $1/48$, not $1/24$, so it is third order.

Steps 1 to 5 are exact (`[C5]`), and the stability polynomials agree with a port of the stage loop (`[C1]`). On a
nonlinear equation the fitted orders are 1.01, 2.01, 3.02 and 3.01 (`[C2]`).

*Strong stability.* In every tableau $w_0^{(s)}+w_1^{(s)}=1$ with $w_0^{(s)},w_1^{(s)}\ge0$, so

$$
\mathbf U^{(s+1)} = w_0^{(s)}\,\mathbf U^n + w_1^{(s)}\Big(\mathbf U^{(s)} + \frac{w_2^{(s)}}{w_1^{(s)}}\,\Delta t\,\mathcal L(\mathbf U^{(s)})\Big) .
$$

6. The stage is a convex combination of $\mathbf U^n$ and a forward-Euler step of size $(w_2^{(s)}/w_1^{(s)})\Delta t$ from
   $\mathbf U^{(s)}$[^rg-4d1d8f105ddf].
7. At the first stage $\mathbf U^{(0)}=\mathbf U^n$, so the whole stage is one forward-Euler step of size
   $w_2^{(0)}\Delta t/(w_0^{(0)}+w_1^{(0)})$.
8. Each stage is therefore safe while its step is at most $\Delta t_{\mathrm{FE}}$, that is for
   $\Delta t\le c^{(s)}_{\mathrm{FE}}\,\Delta t_{\mathrm{FE}}$ with $c^{(0)}_{\mathrm{FE}}=(w_0^{(0)}+w_1^{(0)})/w_2^{(0)}$ and $c^{(s)}_{\mathrm{FE}}=w_1^{(s)}/w_2^{(s)}$ for $s\ge1$.
9. The scheme is safe for $\Delta t\le c_{\mathrm{SSP}}\Delta t_{\mathrm{FE}}$ with $c_{\mathrm{SSP}}=\min_s c^{(s)}_{\mathrm{FE}}$. From
   @tbl-ch07-rk-weights every $c^{(s)}_{\mathrm{FE}}$ is 1 for `rk1`, `rk2` and `rk3`, and every $c^{(s)}_{\mathrm{FE}}$ is 2 for `rk3s4`, so
   $c_{\mathrm{SSP}}$ = 1, 1, 1, 2 (`[C3]`, `[C6]`).

On $\mathrm d\mathcal Y/\mathrm dt=-\mathcal Y$, where forward Euler keeps $\mathcal Y\ge0$ for $\Delta t\le1$, `rk3` keeps it up to 1
and `rk3s4` up to 2 (`[C4]`).[^ch07-rk-ssp] $w_2^{(s)}\le w_1^{(s)}$ is the property the positivity limiter states for every
shipped integrator, in its comment on `wght2` ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.hpp flux_positivity_theta >}}).

[^ch07-rk-ssp]: The argument is that of `sources/canoe__POSITIVITY_TECH_REPORT.md` §3, written out here.

*Round-off.*

10. The average is `wght0() * u0 + wght1() * u1 + wght2() * u2` in the working precision: three products and two
    additions per entry, each rounded once with relative error at most $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2$. The weights
    $\tfrac13$, $\tfrac23$, $\tfrac16$ are not binary fractions, so each weight carries one more rounding.
11. With four roundings on the longest path, the computed entry differs from @eq-ch07-rk-stage by at most
    $\zeta_4\big(\lvert w_0^{(s)}\mathbf U^n\rvert+\lvert w_1^{(s)}\mathbf U^{(s)}\rvert+\lvert w_2^{(s)}\Delta t\,\mathcal L\rvert\big)$, with
    $\zeta_4\approx2\epsilon_{\mathrm m}=4.4\times10^{-16}$ in double, per stage.

The step is first to third order in time as above; the spatial error is that of the operator, @sec-ch04.

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch07-rk-stages for the three stages of `rk3`.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-rk-stages
#| fig-cap: "The three stages of rk3. Sky-blue boxes are the stored states $\\mathbf U^n$, $\\mathbf U^{(1)}$, $\\mathbf U^{(2)}$ and $\\mathbf U^{n+1}$; each black arrow is one stage, labelled with its weights $w_0^{(s)}$, $w_1^{(s)}$, $w_2^{(s)}$ (green) and its full-step increment $w_2^{(s)}\\,\\Delta t\\,\\mathcal L$ (orange). The dashed grey arcs show the step-start state re-entering stages 2 and 3 with weight $w_0^{(s)}$."
#| fig-alt: "Four boxes in a row joined by three arrows with weight labels, and two dashed arcs from the first box to the third and fourth."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.figures.fig_rk_stages import make_fig
make_fig()
```

One stage of `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}) runs, in this order:

1. publish the stage index for the VIC, `rk_stage` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}});
2. at stage 0, save the step-start state `_hydro_u0` and reset the per-step marks and counters
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}); with the implicit radial diffusion of @sec-ch09
   (`implicit_radial`[^rg-311cb1f16924]), its `begin_step`, the physical boundaries and the ghost exchange come first, so the saved
   state is the one after that diffusion step;
3. the hydro tendency, `phydro->forward`, which includes the forcing loop and the VIC
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}});
4. the passive-scalar tendency and the user stage forcings (@sec-ch09); with species and the equation-of-state
   limiter on, the species part of the user forcings' increment is clipped so that it takes no species density below
   zero, nor below what the increment before the user forcings already gave (@sec-ch08; {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}});
5. the average @eq-ch07-rk-stage, at the last stage the implicit radial diffusion's `finish_step` when it is on,
   and the conserved-variable limiter, `apply_conserved_limiter_`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}); on a block with no species and no passive
   scalars the limiter is skipped before the last stage, because the next stage's conversion to primitives applies
   the same pointwise limiter; the scalars get the same average, `_scalar_s0` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}});
6. refill immersed solids; at the last stage, the conserved-variable limiter again, the phase adjustment and the
   gravity-work fixer (@sec-ch06); then the physical boundaries, `apply_boundaries` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).

The scalar tendency of step 4 also carries the VIC's dry-gas face transfer and the scalars' share of any dry-mass
source in the stage (@sec-ch07-vic-redistribute).

Each stage evaluates $\mathcal L$[^rg-323f7dcf8b09] once, so a step costs one, two, three or four operator evaluations. The
averages are tensor arithmetic on whole arrays, ghosts included; the ghosts are rewritten by the boundary fill
and the exchange. Nothing is fused: the dispatch path `call_average3` is commented out
([`pyharp integrator.cpp:109-120`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L109-L120)).

: Code map of the explicit Runge-Kutta stages. {#tbl-ch07-rk-code}

**How to use it.** The integrator is chosen in the `integration`[^rg-fe1c43f1e4de] block, which pyharp's `from_yaml` reads
([`pyharp integrator.cpp:20-31`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L20-L31)):

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `type`[^rg-5a0ce8082ce9].
```yaml
integration:
  type: rk3s4     # rk1 (or euler), rk2, rk3 (default), rk3s4
  cfl: 0.9        # default Courant factor 0.9
```

What is refused, and why:

- An unknown type, for example `rk4`, stops at construction with "Integrator not implemented: requested type 'rk4'",
  because the constructor throws a `runtime_error` for any name but the four
  ([`pyharp integrator.cpp:79-81`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L79-L81)).
- A key in neither snapy's nor pyharp's list stops with its path, so a typo cannot fall back to a default silently.
  `max_redo` is such a key: "unknown key 'integration/max_redo'"
  ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}; Limits 1).

The card, and the two refusals with these messages, were run on a build of the pin.[^ch07-rk-card] The stage of
@eq-ch07-rk-stage is these lines; `u0`, `u1` and `u2` are $\mathbf U^n$, $\mathbf U^{(s)}$ and
$\Delta t\,\mathcal L(\mathbf U^{(s)})$
([`pyharp integrator.cpp:119-120`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L119-L120)):

```cpp
  auto out =
      stages[s].wght0() * u0 + stages[s].wght1() * u1 + stages[s].wght2() * u2;
```

The stage driver calls it as `hydro_u.set_(pintg->forward(stage, _hydro_u0, hydro_u, fut_hydro_du))`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}), so `_hydro_u0` is $\mathbf U^n$ and `fut_hydro_du` is the
full-step increment.

[^ch07-rk-card]: `MeshBlockOptions.from_yaml` and `MeshBlock` on the card with geometry, an ideal-moist equation of
    state, reflecting $x_1$ walls and constant gravity added; snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5 Release
    build, CPU, Python 3.12.10.

: Tests of the explicit Runge-Kutta stages (@tbl-ch07-ctest-run for the run at the pin). {#tbl-ch07-rk-tests}

The ctest cases pass at the pin, except that the reference comparison of `test_straka` was not made
(@tbl-ch07-ctest-run). `rk_check.py` ports the stage formula of `advance_local` and the pyharp weights.[^ch07-rk-run]
`[C1]` evaluates the stage loop on four complex $\mathcal Z$ and matches the four polynomials to $2.2\times10^{-16}$;
`[C2]` fits the orders 1.01, 2.01, 3.02, 3.01 at 40, 80 and 160 steps; `[C3]` finds every stage convex with
$c_{\mathrm{SSP}}$ = 1, 1, 1, 2; `[C4]` keeps $\mathcal Y\ge0$ up to $\Delta t=c_{\mathrm{SSP}}$. `[C5]` checks steps 1 to 5 in
exact arithmetic, `[C6]` every stage fraction $c^{(s)}_{\mathrm{FE}}$, and `[C7]` the two ratios of Limits 3. Coverage: CPU; no CUDA
assertion on the weights.

### Limits

1. **`max_redo` is not a YAML key.** pyharp's `from_yaml` never reads it
   ([`pyharp integrator.cpp:20-31`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L20-L31)), so YAML runs keep the default `max_redo` of 5
   ([`pyharp integrator.hpp:58`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.hpp#L58)); a driver sets it with
   `op.intg().max_redo(n)` before building the block (@sec-ch10-redo).
2. **pyharp is not pinned by snapy's build.** The weights cited here are those of the pyharp commit the report
   cites;[^ch07-rk-pyharp] the property $w_2^{(s)}\le w_1^{(s)}$ that the positivity limiter relies on holds for all four
   tableaux there and must be re-checked against the pyharp a build links.
3. **SSP coefficient of `rk3s4`.** At the same SSP guarantee `rk3s4` takes a step $c_{\mathrm{SSP}}=2$ times that of
   `rk3`, for 4 instead of 3 operator evaluations, so per operator evaluation it advances $2/4$ against $1/3$, 1.5
   times as far (`[C7]`). The time-step bound does not use this: it applies the same `cfl` to every type
   (@sec-ch07-cfl).

[^ch07-rk-pyharp]: pyharp@4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29; pyharp has no `code` shortcode, so its code is
    cited with permalinks at that commit.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-b85b53c55d48]: cfl — Courant-number limit for the time step

[^rg-2b93cd28ee3b]: $C$ — Courant number (named: acoustic, advective, vertical acoustic)

[^rg-15d7eb0a1f99]: $\mathbf U$ — conserved state vector $(\rho_d, m_1, m_2, m_3, E, \rho_1..\rho_{N_y})$

[^rg-a3c1b56ee687]: $\rho_{\mathrm{d}}$ — dry-air density [kg m$^{-3}$]

[^rg-216a5cf9b341]: $\rho_n$ — partial density of species $n$, $\rho y_n$ [kg m$^{-3}$]

[^rg-071a0a3e4354]: $E$ — total energy density, internal plus kinetic, $\rho e + \tfrac12\rho\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2$ [J m$^{-3}$]; excludes potential energy

[^rg-0ebf34f7decd]: YAML — YAML Ain't Markup Language, the structured input format used for decks

[^rg-4d1d8f105ddf]: $\mathbf U^{(s)}$ — state after RK stage $s$; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L817-L825)

[^rg-311cb1f16924]: implicit_radial — whether radial heat conduction on the cubed sphere is solved implicitly, split around the explicit step (default false)

[^rg-323f7dcf8b09]: $\mathcal L$ — the semi-discrete right-hand side (all explicit operators); notation only; see @sec-appa

[^rg-fe1c43f1e4de]: integration — time-integration options

[^rg-5a0ce8082ce9]: type — implementation selector for the enclosing options block
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
